title: RL 串联：电流为什么慢半拍
summary: 电感串电阻接正弦波：用示波器看电流落后电压，再量出三段电压，发现它们不能直接相加。
concepts: 电流落后电压 current lags voltage
相量图 / 电压三角形 phasor diagram
用电阻电压看电流 sense resistor
description: 信号发生器 → L1（10 mH）→ VR → R1（100 Ω）→ GND，1.6 kHz 正弦波。CH2 在电阻上，看到的就是电流的波形；把 CH2 夹到电感两端读 v_L，用三段电压检查交流 KVL。

cards.title: 两条正弦波，谁先到顶？
text: 信号发生器设成 **正弦波、`1.6 kHz`、幅度 `1 V`**。CH1 看加上去的电压；CH2 看电阻上的电压——电阻上的电压和流过它的电流同一个形状。
看两条波形：CH2 的波峰比 CH1 **早**到还是**晚**到？

cards.title: 电感讨厌变化
text: - 电感会顶住电流的**变化**。所以电流跟不上电压，总是**晚一点**才到顶。
![](fig:waves)
- 频率越高，变化越快，电感顶得越狠。这种“交流里的电阻”叫**感抗**：
$$X_L = 2\pi f L$$
- 两段电压不是同时到顶的，所以不能直接相加。把每个电压画成一支箭头（**相量**，长度取有效值）：电阻的箭头沿着电流，电感的箭头**超前四分之一圈**。加上去的电压是三角形的斜边。
![](fig:triangle)

cards.title: 量出三角形的三条边
text: - 先保持 CH2 在电阻上：读 CH1、CH2 的 **Vpp**，再读示波器下面的 **CH2 相对 CH1 的相位差**。
- 再把 **CH2 夹到电感两端**：针尖插 **`d3`**，接地夹插 **`d10`**。这里的探头量的是“针尖减接地夹”，所以 CH2 显示的就是电感电压 v_L。
- 电路检查通过后填测量题。填完可以把频率换成 `160 Hz` 和 `16 kHz`，看落后的角度怎么变。

cards.title: 带走
text: - 电感里**电流落后电压**。频率越高，$X_L$ 越大，落后得越多。
- 交流电压按**相量**（箭头）相加，不能把读数直接加。本课程的相量一律用**有效值**。
- 坑：真实示波器的接地夹连着市电的地线。把它夹在电感两端，等于把 R1 那头短接到地。真实电路里要用两个通道都对地测，再相减。
- 真实的 10 mH 小电感有几欧到几十欧的线圈电阻（这里按 1 Ω 算），落后的角度会小一些。

caption.text: 电压先到顶，电流（CH2）晚一点才到顶：电流落后电压。

i18n.en: The voltage peaks first and the current (CH2) a little later: the current lags the voltage.

caption.text: 相量三角形：V_R 沿着电流，V_L 超前 90°，加上去的电压 V_in 是斜边——它比 V_R + V_L 短。

i18n.en: The phasor triangle: V_R along the current, V_L 90° ahead, and the applied V_in is the long side — shorter than V_R + V_L.

en.title: Series RL: why the current is late
en.summary: An inductor and a resistor on a sine: watch the current lag the voltage on the scope, then measure three voltages and find they do not simply add.
concepts: seeing current through a sense resistor
en.description: Generator → L1 (10 mH) → VR → R1 (100 Ω) → GND on a 1.6 kHz sine. CH2 across the resistor shows the current; clipping CH2 across the inductor gives v_L, and the three voltages check AC KVL.
compare: - At f = 1.6 kHz: X_L = 2π × 1600 × 10 mH ≈ 100.5 Ω ≈ R + r = 101 Ω. The current I = V_in/Z lags V_in by arctan(X_L/(R + r)) ≈ 45°; V_R/V_in = R/|Z| ≈ 100/142.5 ≈ 0.70.

- **Voltage triangle**: V_in = V_R + V_L as (rms) phasors, with V_L about 90° ahead of V_R. On the scope VIN ≈ 1.57 Vpp (the 50 Ω output resistance takes a share, see below), v_R ≈ 1.10 Vpp, v_L ≈ 1.11 Vpp: 1.10 + 1.11 = 2.21 ≠ 1.57, but √(1.10² + 1.11²) ≈ 1.56 ≈ 1.57. **KVL in AC circuits adds phasors, not RMS or peak-to-peak values.**
- RMS current I = (1 V/√2) / |151 + j100.5| Ω ≈ 3.9 mA (count the 50 Ω here, because the 1 V is the generator's internal EMF).

**Why VIN is only 1.57 Vpp**: the generator's 1 V is the amplitude of its internal ideal source, which reaches the terminals through 50 Ω. Terminal voltage = 1 V × |Z| / |Z + 50 Ω| = 142.5 / |151 + j100.5| ≈ 0.786 V peak. Using the terminal voltage (CH1) as the reference for gain and phase removes this effect.
- 160 Hz: X_L ≈ 10 Ω ≪ R, almost a purely resistive circuit; the current is nearly in phase with the voltage (≈ 5.7° behind), v_R/v_in ≈ 0.985 (= 100/101 × 0.995: the coil's 1 Ω takes 1%).
- 16 kHz: X_L ≈ 1005 Ω ≫ R; the current is small and ≈ 84° behind, v_R/v_in ≈ 0.10, and almost all the voltage is across the inductor.
**Think about it**: taking v_R as the output, this circuit is an **RL low-pass filter** with cutoff fc = (R + r)/(2πL) ≈ 1.6 kHz.

measurements.ask: 1.6 kHz: CH1 (VIN, the generator terminals) Vpp
measurements.explain: The 1 V is the generator's internal EMF, which reaches the terminals through 50 Ω: 2 × 1 V × 142.5 / |151 + j100.5| ≈ 1.57 Vpp.

measurements.ask: 1.6 kHz: CH2 (v_R, the current's waveform) Vpp
1.6 kHz: phase of CH2 on the resistor (the current) relative to CH1 (lagging is negative)
measurements.explain: The current lags by arctan(X_L/(R + r)) ≈ arctan(100.5/101) ≈ 45°. This frequency is the RL low-pass cutoff fc = (R + r)/(2πL).

measurements.ask: 1.6 kHz: CH2 across the inductor (tip d3, clip d10), the Vpp of the inductor voltage v_L
measurements.explain: X_L = 2π × 1600 × 10 mH ≈ 100.5 Ω ≈ R + r, so v_L is about as big as v_R, ≈ 1.11 Vpp.

measurements.ask: Check KVL with your three readings:
measurements.explain: 1.10 + 1.11 = 2.21 ≠ 1.57, but √(1.10² + 1.11²) ≈ 1.56. AC KVL adds phasors: V_L leads V_R by about 90°.
choices: VIN ≈ √(V_R² + V_L²): phasors add, about 90° apart
VIN ≈ V_R + V_L: they simply add

hints: Inductor first (in the red clip's column), then the resistor to GND.
A resistor's voltage has the shape and phase of its current: CH2 on the resistor shows the current.
X_L = 2πfL; at 1.6 kHz that is about 100 Ω, close to R.
tests: 1.6 kHz: the current (v_R) lags VIN; sensible RMS current
1.6 kHz: the peak-to-peak v_R, v_L and VIN add as phasors

cards.title: Two sines: which one peaks first?
text: The generator and both probes are already on the board. **Inductor** (`10 mH`) into **`b3`**–**`b10`**, **resistor** (`100 Ω`) into **`c10`**–**`tn10`**.
Set the generator to **sine, `1.6 kHz`, amplitude `1 V`**. CH1 shows the voltage you apply; CH2 shows the voltage across the resistor — and a resistor's voltage has the same shape as its current.
Look at the two traces: does CH2 reach its top **before** CH1 or **after** it?

cards.title: An inductor hates change
text: - An inductor pushes back against any **change** of current. So the current cannot keep up with the voltage: it always peaks a little **later**.
![](fig:waves)
- The higher the frequency, the faster the change and the harder the inductor pushes back. This "AC resistance" is the **inductive reactance**:
$$X_L = 2\pi f L$$
At 1.6 kHz: $X_L = 2\pi × 1600 × 0.01 ≈ 100$ Ω, about the same as R.

- The two voltages do not peak at the same moment, so they do not simply add. Draw each one as an arrow (a **phasor**, its length the rms value): the resistor's arrow points along the current, the inductor's is **a quarter turn ahead**. The applied voltage is the long side of the triangle.
![](fig:triangle)

cards.title: Measure the three sides
text: - Keep CH2 on the resistor first: read the **Vpp** of CH1 and CH2, then the **phase of CH2 vs CH1** under the scope screen.
- Then **clip CH2 across the inductor**: tip into **`d3`**, ground clip into **`d10`**. These probes measure tip minus clip, so CH2 now shows the inductor voltage v_L.
- Once the circuit check passes, fill in the questions. Afterwards try `160 Hz` and `16 kHz` and watch how the lag changes.

cards.title: Take away
text: - In an inductor **the current lags the voltage**. The higher the frequency, the bigger $X_L$ and the bigger the lag.
- AC voltages add as **phasors** (arrows), not as plain readings. Phasors in this course are always **rms** values.
- Pitfall: a real scope's ground clip is tied to mains earth. Clip it across the inductor and you short R1's end to ground. On a real bench, measure both channels to ground and subtract.
- A real 10 mH coil has a few to tens of ohms of winding resistance (this one has 1 Ω), so the lag comes out a little smaller.

tests.name: 1.6 kHz：电流（v_R）落后 VIN；电流有效值合理
1.6 kHz：v_R、v_L、VIN 的峰峰值按相量相加

compare: - **电压三角形**：V̇in = V̇R + V̇L（有效值相量），而 V̇L 超前 V̇R 约 90°。示波器上 VIN ≈ 1.57 Vpp（50 Ω 输出电阻分掉了一部分，见下）、v_R ≈ 1.10 Vpp、v_L ≈ 1.11 Vpp：1.10 + 1.11 = 2.21 ≠ 1.57，但 √(1.10² + 1.11²) ≈ 1.56 ≈ 1.57。**交流电路的 KVL 是相量相加，不是有效值 / 峰峰值直接相加**。
- 电流有效值 I = 1 V/√2 / |151 + j100.5| Ω ≈ 3.9 mA（这里要把 50 Ω 算进去，因为 1 V 是信号发生器内部的电动势）。
**为什么 VIN 只有 1.57 Vpp**：信号发生器的 1 V 是它内部理想源的幅度，经过 50 Ω 才到端子。端子电压 = 1 V × |Z| / |Z + 50 Ω| = 142.5 / |151 + j100.5| ≈ 0.786 V 峰值。测滤波器、相位时都拿端子电压（CH1）作参考，这个影响就消掉了。
- 160 Hz：X_L ≈ 10 Ω ≪ R，几乎是纯电阻电路，电流几乎和电压同相（落后 ≈ 5.7°），v_R/v_in ≈ 0.985（= 100/101 × 0.995，线圈的 1 Ω 分走了 1%）。
- 16 kHz：X_L ≈ 1005 Ω ≫ R，电流很小且落后 ≈ 84°，v_R/v_in ≈ 0.10，几乎全部电压都在电感上。
**想一想**：这个电路取 v_R 作输出，就是一个 **RL 低通滤波器**，截止频率 fc = (R + r)/(2πL) ≈ 1.6 kHz。

measurements.ask: 1.6 kHz：CH1（VIN，信号发生器端子）的 Vpp
measurements.explain: 1 V 是信号发生器内部的电动势，经过 50 Ω 才到端子：2 × 1 V × 142.5 / |151 + j100.5| ≈ 1.57 Vpp。

measurements.ask: 1.6 kHz：CH2（v_R，也就是电流的波形）的 Vpp
1.6 kHz：CH2 在电阻上（电流）相对 CH1 的相位差（落后为负）
measurements.explain: 电流落后 arctan(X_L/(R + r)) ≈ arctan(100.5/101) ≈ 45°。这个频率就是 RL 低通的截止频率 fc = (R + r)/(2πL)。

measurements.ask: 1.6 kHz：CH2 夹到电感两端（针尖 d3、接地夹 d10），读电感电压 v_L 的 Vpp
measurements.explain: X_L = 2π × 1600 × 10 mH ≈ 100.5 Ω ≈ R + r，所以 v_L 和 v_R 差不多大，≈ 1.11 Vpp。

choices: VIN ≈ √(V_R² + V_L²)：相量相加，两者相差约 90°
measurements.ask: 用你的三个读数检查 KVL：

hints: 电感在前（接红夹子那一列），电阻在后接 GND。
电阻上的电压和电流同形状、同相位：CH2 在电阻上，看到的就是电流。
X_L = 2πfL，1.6 kHz 时约 100 Ω，和 R 差不多。
